questions.q: Why does the migration create two separate Knowledge Bases instead of one?
options: To separate end-user-facing content from internal IT runbooks, each with its own Can Read / Can Contribute audience
Because a single Knowledge Base cannot technically hold more than a few hundred articles
Because Workflow state only functions when more than one Knowledge Base exists
To avoid using the Category field at all
questions.explain: Self-Service and IT Staff content need different audiences, decided at the Knowledge Base container level.

questions.q: In the lab's approval flow, what state does every migrated article start in, regardless of how polished the original Word document was?
options: Draft
Published
Retired
Review
questions.explain: A document nobody has reviewed inside ServiceNow's own workflow hasn't actually been reviewed yet, so it starts in Draft.

questions.q: What happens when the Knowledge manager rejects an article during the approval step?
options: The flow returns it to Draft with the reviewer's comments attached, so the author knows exactly what to fix
The article is immediately deleted along with its history
The article is published anyway with a warning
The flow has no rejection path and the record stays stuck in Review forever
questions.explain: Rejection is a real feedback loop back to Draft, not a dead end or a silent failure.

questions.q: What does the quarterly review job in Step 3 actually check for?
options: Published articles whose last updated date is 12 months or more in the past
Only articles that have already been Retired
Articles with a Category field set to blank
Articles that have never received any Helpful votes
questions.explain: The scheduled job flags articles that have gone stale by time, not just by negative feedback.

questions.q: Why does the lab build the two Knowledge Bases before the approval flow, rather than the other way around?
options: Because the approval flow needs a clear answer for who the approver is, and Self-Service and IT Staff content often need different reviewers
Order doesn't actually matter for this implementation
Because Flow Designer cannot reference a Knowledge Base that was created after the flow
Because Workflow state cannot exist until a Knowledge Base is created
questions.explain: Audience segmentation has to exist first so the approval routing has somewhere real to route to.
